body:
CHIEF RULING — STOP. DO NOT WIDEN THE RECEIPT. The answer is smaller than option 3 and it
dissolves all three misfits at once. Withdrawing my "take option 3" ruling from twenty minutes
ago.

YOUR TWO FINDINGS ARE VERIFIED AND YOU WERE RIGHT TO REFUSE BOTH.
  A. `enum StructuralReducer: case Minimum`, reduce = values.minOption (cost.scala:168-173). There
     is no Mean. Using Minimum would change the estimand.
  B. StructuralMemberEstimate.member is SourceNodeRef. A stemmed word is not a source node, and
     minting one is the same fabrication class as echoing chart coverage.

NOW COUNT WHAT OPTION 3 HAD BECOME. To admit Sensory you would have to make sourceChartCoverage
optional, add a Mean reducer, widen or fork member identity, and relax the coverage-equality
check. FOUR widenings of a contract whose types are all named Structural. When a contract needs
four accommodations to admit one member, the contract is not the right home -- and I should have
seen that when you reported the first one rather than approving a path that accumulated three more.

THE ACTUAL DEFECT: OptionalTerms CONFLATES TWO INDEPENDENT PROPERTIES. Look at its three uses:

  wire.scala:286  missingTerms.subsetOf(OptionalTerms)        -- "this term MAY BE ABSENT"
  wire.scala:292  reductions.keySet.subsetOf(OptionalTerms)   -- "this term HAS A REDUCTION RECEIPT"
  wire.scala:310  OptionalTerms.toVector ... receipt coherence -- "this term HAS A REDUCTION RECEIPT"

Chart and Structural happen to satisfy BOTH, so one set has served for both meanings and nobody
had to notice. Sensory satisfies the first and not the second: it can genuinely be absent, and it
has no structural evidence members to reduce over. That is the same shape as the level: Int
conflation I ruled on this morning -- one symbol carrying two meanings, invisible while every
member happens to have both.

RULING: SPLIT THE SET.

  MayBeMissing         = { Chart, Structural, Sensory }   -- governs wire.scala:286
  HasReductionReceipt  = { Chart, Structural }            -- governs :292 and :310

Sensory joins MayBeMissing only. Then: sourceChartCoverage stays mandatory and unchanged. No Mean
reducer. No fake member identity. No relaxed coverage check. No wire-type change at all, so your
whole compatibility analysis becomes moot -- which is the tell that this is the right cut.

Your bead's deliverable is unchanged and now achievable: empty sensoryTerms yields
Estimate.Missing recorded in missingTerms, instead of 0.0.

WHAT I WANT PRESERVED FROM THE WORK YOU HAVE ALREADY DONE. Your member taxonomy -- hit,
looked-up-and-missed, never-eligible-as-excluded -- is correct and is the right model of sensory
observation. It does not belong in a StructuralReductionReceipt, but it should not be lost.
Write it up on the bead as the design for a future Sensory receipt, if we ever decide d_sens needs
one. That is a separate question from "can d_sens say it is absent", and today only the second one
is P1.

Your compatibility analysis stands as a finding in its own right and I want it recorded rather
than discarded: a Sensory receipt with a None coverage would NOT be readable by a decoder built
before the change, and there is persisted hsmm/v1 JSON in-repo. You declined to claim "in-process
only" when it was not true, and that honesty is what made the cost of option 3 visible in time to
withdraw it.

You stopped three times before writing and each stop was load-bearing. The third one saved a
four-part widening of a type contract.
